Result: ruff format, ruff check and mypy passed; **pytest reached its footer `= 123 failed, 11837 passed, 1137 skipped, 2241 warnings, 6 errors, 42 subtests passed in 4027.85s (1:07:07) =`**, make printed `make: *** [Makefile:28: check] Error 1` and returned 2, `capture_script` returned rc 2, and the bootstrap's own `numeric_counts` on the log's last 64 KB returned **`{}`** — the public-style summary is `{"command": "check", "counts": {}, "exit_code": 2}`, byte-for-byte the signature of both hosted key-using runs. Peak container memory 2.26 GiB; no abnormal marker. **Demonstrated cause** (`scripts/ci_private_inputs.py:265-278`): `numeric_counts` accepts only lines that `startswith("===")` AND `endswith("===")`; pytest pads its final summary line with `=` to the terminal width (80 columns when stdout is not a TTY, as under capture and on hosted), and when the summary text is longer than that width it emits a single `=` on each side — every full-suite footer of this repository (hundreds of failures, skips, warnings, errors, subtests and the `(h:mm:ss)` duration suffix for runs over a minute) is longer, so the parser never matches it; short footers (`====== 3 failed, 10 passed in 1.23s ======`) match, which is why the qualification probes passed. Verified with the real function: the captured footer → `{}`; `= 5 passed in 70.00s (0:01:10) =` → `{}`; `====== 3 failed, 10 passed in 1.23s ======` → `{failed: 3, passed: 10}`. **H ruling on the comparison-run-3 findings F1–F5: F1 is a defect against design §A.5 (correction α in a separate re-reviewed packet H3-7); F2 is the intended reading (the 12 rows become hermetic); F3 defines the CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN inapplicability class; F4 is a test-seam correction; run 4 after H3-7 fixes the closed list (ruling 04:58–05:00 UTC 2026-10-19; recorded 05:01 UTC).** Request `h3-run3-findings-prompt-01.txt` (SHA256 277925d7…, 1,285 words). Ruling `cir04h3-run3-findings-ruling.json` (SHA256 357e7ba0657dc83e4c38dcfed0757c718d5eca100e5d8ababb902091c22ad244; 138 s; $69.59; read poppler_linux_runtime.py:238-260, strict_launcher.py:997-1012, pdf.py:886-905, ocr_health.py:241-345 in the H3 worktree; relied on the request for the ocr.py call sites, worker.py:1676-1687, real_example_gate.py:737-748 and the row diffs). F1 (defect): `install_poppler_child_environment` mutates os.environ and calls chdir whenever `apply_to_process` is true, which is the default, and nothing guarantees the caller is the child. Correction (α): all Linux renders happen inside the dedicated child, enforced in code — `apply_to_process` keyword-only with no default; `True` raises `PopplerRuntimeBindingError("POPPLER_RUNTIME_PARENT_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN")` unless inside a governed worker child (`multiprocessing.parent_process() is not None` AND a child marker set by the worker entry); pdf.py:1229 and :1510 keep True; ocr.py:1078, :2398, :2558, :3093 may apply only inside the worker child launched by the transport (any inline caller fails closed); tests that call worker bodies inline (including the seven test_ocr_batched_file_worker nodes) drive the real child or inject an explicit child seam; ocr_health.py:254 stays False. (β) rejected: os.environ is global and the page OCR runs under a ThreadPoolExecutor, so a lock serialises renders but not other threads' subprocesses (tesseract, ffmpeg, uvicorn), and a process-wide mapping violates §A.5. The mapping stays (pdf2image copies os.environ and prepends poppler_path to LD_LIBRARY_PATH; an empty variable leaves an empty component, i.e. the cwd is searched; DT_RPATH binds only the prefix libraries); the chdir is not needed for loader safety once the mapping is present, is harmless defence inside the guarded child, and is never allowed in a parent. REDs: on Linux with the prefix the parent's os.environ and cwd are byte-identical before and after a public in-process OCR or PDF call; apply_to_process=True in the parent raises; the signature has no default; the loader negative still passes; the health path never mutates the process. F2 (intended): acceptance-v1 is the canonical acceptance profile and CI health uses bootstrap-v1, so refusing an acceptance-v1 worker when the resolver admits the Linux prefix keeps non-canonical identity out of acceptance evidence; worker.py:1687 and real_example_gate.py:748 are defence in depth. The 12 rows are host-sensitive tests, not product defects: each monkeypatches `resolve_pinned_poppler_runtime` to raise POPPLER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE, plus one positive pin that a stubbed PinnedLinuxPopplerRuntime makes the launcher raise POPPLER_RUNTIME_NONCANONICAL before polling; they join no gate. F3 (canonical by construction): `build_pdf_ocr_render_admissions` is the acceptance gate's own public constructor and accepts only the Windows PinnedPopplerRuntime; do not widen it; those rows can never pass on Linux; class CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN on the item (k) model — decorator `requires_canonical_poppler_pin`, token `CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN NOT_EXECUTED: Windows byte pin absent`, JUnit property `canonical_poppler_pin`, required-mode variable `IDIS_REQUIRE_CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN=1`, closed tuple `CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN_GATED_NODES` with an AST census; keyed on the resolver returning anything other than an exact PinnedPopplerRuntime (on a Windows host with the pin present the rows execute; any binding error other than UNAVAILABLE there fails); the only acceptance evidence is the owner's Windows present-mode run at the final head citing pin identity 8ebfb07d…. F5 joins the class only if each of its three tracebacks shows the refusal originating at pdf.py:901-905 or another Windows-pin check in the gate path; otherwise it stays a red finding to diagnose. F4: the Linux health decision is correct as written (PATH Poppler never trusted on Linux; the injected binary_resolver must not be honoured for Poppler there); the two tests move to the existing `poppler_runtime_probe` seam on Linux (raising POPPLER_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE, expecting MISSING_DEPENDENCIES ["poppler"], deduplicated) and keep binary_resolver on non-Linux via a platform monkeypatch. Run 3 is not the reference: run 4 after H3-7 fixes `LINUX_POPPLER_GATED_NODES` from rows red in run 2 and green in run 4, and must show the ~88 chdir-tainted rows green, the 12 F2 rows green through the seam, the F4 rows green, the CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN rows NOT_EXECUTED and nothing new red. Packet: H3-7 (F1, the F2 and F4 seams, the F1 REDs) is separate, re-reviewed, implemented in the H3 worktree after H3-4 finishes; the CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN gate (F3, F5 if confirmed) goes with the closed-list gate packet; publication is H3-3 + H3-4 + H3-7 + the gate packet together, nothing of H3 before. Verbatim: "F1: install_poppler_child_environment's process mutation is a defect against design §A.5; correction (α): apply_to_process keyword-only without default, True only inside a governed worker child (parent_process() set and a child marker), otherwise POPPLER_RUNTIME_PARENT_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN; pdf.py:1229/:1510 keep True; ocr.py call sites only inside the transport's child; parent os.environ and cwd proven unchanged." "F2: refusing acceptance-v1 workers on an admitted Linux prefix is intended (canonical profile); the 12 rows become hermetic via a resolver seam plus one NONCANONICAL pin." "F3 (and F5 if its tracebacks confirm): CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN class — build_pdf_ocr_render_admissions stays Windows-only; the decorator, token 'CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN NOT_EXECUTED: Windows byte pin absent', property canonical_poppler_pin, IDIS_REQUIRE_CANONICAL_POPPLER_PIN=1 and a closed tuple; acceptance only from the owner's Windows present-mode run at the final head."
